summary:
Field Shift: Satellite-Driven Crop Rotation & Resilience Planner is a user-friendly web decision support system that provides information to farmers on how best to rotate crops on their farms to accommodate changes in climatic conditions year after year.

The online portal combines 10-year earth observation data from NASA including SMAP, root-zone soil moisture, GPM extreme precipitation and runoff, ECOSTRESS vegetation water stress and POWER agro-climatology data with local soil characteristics and crop properties. The users can weigh various factors such as water management, soil conservation, profit variability, and pest breaks to assess four years of customized rotation strategies relative to the current strategy. Users also have the option to substitute crops and stress test their chosen crop rotation strategy through the portal.

With the translation of earth observation satellite databases into simple language suggestions for the growers’ fields, Field Shift enables growers to preserve topsoils, conserve water, minimize the use of chemical fertilizers and build farm sustainability.
details:
🌱 Field Shift – Helping Farmers Make Smarter Decisions

Field Shift is a web app that helps farmers plan which crops to grow over the next four years. Nowadays, climate change is making farming more difficult because of changing rainfall, rising temperatures, and water shortages. Our idea is to help farmers prepare for these challenges and make better decisions.

The app uses the last 10 years of NASA satellite data (2016–2026), along with local soil details, to understand the farming conditions.

Farmers can enter information about their soil and choose what they want to focus on, such as saving water, improving soil health, earning a steady income, or reducing pest problems. Based on their choices, Field Shift suggests three different crop rotation plans: Water-Saver, Soil-Builder, and Balanced Resilience. It also compares these plans with the farmer's current farming method.

One useful feature is that farmers can check how their crop plans might perform during difficult weather conditions, like a 2°C rise in temperature or a 30% drop in summer rainfall. They can also change crops and see how it affects water usage, soil health, and profit. Once they are happy with the plan, they can download it as a PDF or CSV file.

🌍 Impact

Our main aim is to make farming information easier to understand and use. Instead of showing complicated satellite data, the app gives farmers simple alerts and clear crop recommendations.

In water-stressed conditions, our model shows the potential to reduce irrigation requirements by up to 46%. It also suggests growing legumes and cover crops, which can improve soil quality, prevent soil erosion, and reduce fertilizer expenses.

We considered different farming conditions while developing this idea, including farms in the U.S. High Plains and small farms in Kerala, India.

💻 Technologies Used

  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Chart.js
  • NASA SMAP, GPM, ECOSTRESS and POWER data
  • ISRIC SoilGrids

🎨 Design and User Experience

We wanted to make the app simple enough for farmers to use without needing technical knowledge. The main screen shows important information like water requirements, soil condition, and suggested crops instead of complicated scientific data.

Farmers are free to change the suggested crops according to their needs. Another important feature is that the app works offline, so it can still be used in areas where internet connectivity is poor.

Our Vision

We believe farming should be prepared for the future, not just the present. Through Field Shift, we want to help farmers save water, improve soil health, reduce farming risks, and make better crop decisions even as the climate changes.
